reviewScope: Review only. This review does not mark DR-112 SATISFIED, does not qualify or demonstrate anything, does not authorize implementation, and does not apply or seal the candidate.
summary: The v4 security and machine repairs are substantial and pass the dispatched attacks: authenticated payloadKind makes ordinary/recovery PRESENT guards disjoint; only one ST-RECOVERY/PRESENT member remains; recoveryTyped UNBOOTSTRAPPED input stages only; RECOVER-COMMIT invokes a full recoveryTrustedEntry with positive authority, old/new/role binding, envelope/time/freshness, threshold, and anti-rollback checks; executable INSTALL/CONTINUE refusals carry closed reasons; accepted abort uses a separate ceremonyTermination record; the inherited and live COORD pins are distinguished and reproduce. Acceptance is withheld for one successor-integrity defect: appliesFindingsOf says the Codex v3 verdict had zero advisories and notFoldedThisSuccessor is empty, but the permitted verdict contains SITCV3-A1 and v4 retains its undeclared 'computed' target unchanged. Two nonblocking advisories cover the deferred replay row's unused reason identity and ambiguous DR-103 envelope attribution. At 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, DR-112 remains OPEN and this verdict authorizes no implementation.

shouldFix.title: The successor ledger silently drops the Codex v3 advisory and falsely records zero advisories
shouldFix.measurement: The permitted Codex v3 verdict reproduces at 45b04bf3... and declares advisoryCount=1 with SITCV3-A1, 'EV-RECOVER-ABORT uses an undeclared transition-target token'. v4's codexV3 record instead says advisories: [], its idCollisionNote lists only the two blockers and one SHOULD-FIX, basedOn.method names only CODEX-V3-B1/B2 and CODEX-V3-S1, and notFoldedThisSuccessor is empty. The underlying datum is unchanged after transition deletion/reindexing: EV-RECOVER-ABORT still has to='computed', neither a declared state id nor the established 'same' meta-target.
shouldFix.whyShouldFix: The predecessor advisory itself is nonblocking, but the successor's evidence ledger makes an objectively false claim about a digest-pinned verdict and silently represents the still-unrepaired finding as folded. Independent-review provenance must distinguish 'repaired', 'carried advisory', and 'not read'; otherwise notFoldedThisSuccessor and finding counts cannot be audited.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Record the predecessor finding under a qualified identity such as CODEX-V3-A1 in codexV3.advisories and notFoldedThisSuccessor, and state that it remains advisory; or replace 'computed' with a structured target function/explicit guarded state rows and record the advisory as repaired. Do not rewrite the v3 verdict.

advisories.title: The deferred replay reason is in the closed vocabulary but is not attached to the replay row
advisories.detail: CONTINUE-REPLAY-NOT-DESIGNED is minted in refusalReasonVocabulary, but its only apparent consumer—the 'newly revoked REPLAY component' row—still yields alreadyRunning='not designed' and newProcess='not designed' with no outcome or refusalReason. This is not acceptance-blocking because offlineRunningPolicy.scope and FC-REPLAY-NAMED explicitly exclude replay from executable v4 behavior and defer it to DR-113, so no permissive result is created. Either attach the code to an explicit fail-closed attempted-event disposition, or mark the vocabulary member reserved-for-DR-113/remove it until that owner activates.

advisories.title: RECOVER-COMMIT ambiguously attributes envelope verification to DR-103
advisories.detail: The transition guard says 'DR-103 byte/envelope verification'. Read literally, the DR-103 modifier covers both checks, although the artifact's detailed recoveryTrustedEntry, recoveryCeremony, and ID-DEP-T1 correctly leave only UNSIGNED/DIGEST_MISMATCH byte checks to DR-103 and keep envelope validity in DR-112 after ID-DEP-1 activation. The detailed definitions make the intended ownership recoverable, so this is advisory; rewrite the shorthand as 'DR-103 active byte-level checks plus DR-112 envelope verification' to remove the conflicting reading.
